methodological_rigor.justification: This is a retrospective multicenter cohort using diagnostic FFPE biopsies from 119 treatment-naive de novo follicular lymphoma patients (2002-2022) plus 16 de novo transformed cases, with an additional 25 paired diagnosis-relapse samples, relating panel-derived TMB to PFS/LSS/OS and POD24 (Methods 2.1-2.2). TMB estimation and filtering criteria (panel size, depth, VAF/read-depth cutoffs, and germline filtering) are described in detail, which supports analytic validity (Methods 2.4). The statistical plan uses nonparametric comparisons with correction where applicable, Cox proportional hazards modeling with assumption checks and model-performance metrics, and an empirically derived cutoff via maximally selected rank statistics (Methods 2.6), but residual confounding and treatment heterogeneity remain inherent limitations of the retrospective design.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The study is an individual retrospective cohort assessing prognosis in frontline-treated follicular lymphoma, which fits Oxford LoE 2b. The endpoints are clinically meaningful (PFS, lymphoma-specific survival, overall survival, and POD24), and the work aims to improve risk stratification beyond existing indices by adding a molecular biomarker (Abstract; Methods 2.2). While not interventional, the findings could inform follow-up intensity and trial stratification if externally validated.

reporting_quality.justification: REMARK is the best fit given the prognostic biomarker focus, and the manuscript reports cohort assembly, treatment context, endpoint definitions, assay platform, and a transparent statistical strategy including cutoff derivation and Cox modeling (Methods 2.1-2.6). It also provides cohort-level response and survival summaries with confidence intervals (Results 3.1). Data and code availability are not described in the normalized manuscript, and there is no explicit statement of public deposition for sequencing or analysis scripts, limiting reproducibility to what can be reimplemented from text.

novelty_literature.justification: The manuscript's main contribution is evaluating targeted-panel TMB as a prognostic biomarker in follicular lymphoma and relating it to POD24 and survival outcomes with an empirically chosen cutoff (>2.55 mut/Mb) (Abstract; Methods 2.6). It extends TMB's established role in other cancers and in immunotherapy contexts to an indolent lymphoma prognosis setting, which is a meaningful but not field-defining step. The work also adds a small paired diagnosis-relapse analysis suggesting relative TMB stability over time (Abstract; Results discussion of relapse samples).

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well structured with clear definitions of outcomes (PFS/LSS/OS and POD24) and a stepwise description of the sequencing/TMB workflow and statistical approach (Methods 2.2-2.6). Results are reported with quantitative summaries (e.g., response rates, median PFS with 95% CI) and use consistent terminology across sections (Results 3.1). Overall clarity is good, though the methods are dense and could benefit from more signposting of the modified TMB workflow steps.

key_strengths: Clinically meaningful prognostic endpoints (PFS, LSS, OS and POD24) defined and analyzed in a sizable de novo FL cohort (Methods 2.2; Results 3.1).
Detailed description of TMB estimation from a 409-gene panel, including depth/quality thresholds and germline filtering (Methods 2.4).
Appropriate statistical methodology for prognostic work, including Cox models with assumption checks and a data-driven cutoff method (Methods 2.6).
key_concerns: Retrospective design and heterogeneous frontline regimens/maintenance introduce potential confounding that may not be fully addressed by modeling (Methods 2.1).
A key analysis subset (mutational profiling for m7-FLIPI) is available only for 64/119 patients, which may limit generalizability of those comparisons (Methods 2.5).
No explicit data/code availability statement is present in the normalized manuscript, limiting external reproducibility and validation.
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a methodologically solid prognostic biomarker analysis with clinically relevant outcomes and generally strong reporting; it would plausibly be accepted in a tier-2 oncology/hematology venue after modest clarifications around confounding, subsets, and reproducibility.
